Compare DPP Between Two Procedures

Source: R/dpp_functions.R
compare_dpp.Rd

Computes average DPP for two lineup procedures and tests their difference with a nonparametric bootstrap, as Smith et al. (2019) did.

Usage

compare_dpp(
  data_proc_a,
  data_proc_b,
  lineup_size = 6,
  alpha = NULL,
  beta = NULL,
  n_bootstrap = 1000,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL,
  innocent_suspect = "auto"
)

Arguments

data_proc_a

Dataframe for procedure A (standard lineup format)

data_proc_b

Dataframe for procedure B (standard lineup format)

lineup_size

Integer. Lineup size (default = 6)

alpha, beta

Optional Equation 3 weights; see make_dpp.

n_bootstrap

Integer. Number of bootstrap samples (default = 1000). Use 0 to skip the bootstrap.

conf_level

Numeric. Confidence level for the interval (default = 0.95)

seed

Integer. Random seed for reproducibility (default = NULL)

innocent_suspect

How innocent-suspect identifications in target-absent lineups are obtained. "designated": the lineups had a designated innocent suspect, so target-absent "suspect" rows are counted directly, and zero such rows means a false-ID rate of zero. "estimated": there was no designated innocent suspect, so the innocent-suspect count is estimated as filler IDs divided by lineup_size. "auto" (the default) chooses "designated" when any target-absent row is a suspect ID or the data have a non-missing suspect_pos column, and "estimated" otherwise, with a message.

Value

An object of class "lineup_dpp_comparison", a list containing:

  • dpp_a: Average DPP for procedure A

  • dpp_b: Average DPP for procedure B

  • dpp_difference: DPP_A - DPP_B (negative = A is better)

  • se_difference: Bootstrap standard error of the difference

  • ci_difference: Percentile bootstrap interval for the difference

  • boot_differences: Bootstrap distribution of the difference

  • dpp_obj_a, dpp_obj_b: Full make_dpp() objects

  • n_bootstrap, conf_level: Settings used

Details

Lower DPP indicates better performance, so a negative difference means procedure A is better. Each bootstrap replicate resamples target-present and target-absent trials separately within each procedure, so every replicate keeps the original design, and the two procedures are treated as independent samples. The innocent-suspect design and the confidence criteria are determined once on each full dataset and reused in every replicate, so every replicate averages over the same criteria.

References

Smith, A. M., Lampinen, J. M., Wells, G. L., Smalarz, L., & Mackovichova, S. (2019). Deviation from perfect performance measures the diagnostic utility of eyewitness lineups but partial area under the ROC curve does not. Journal of Applied Research in Memory and Cognition, 8(1), 50-59. doi:10.1016/j.jarmac.2018.09.003

Examples

data(lineup_example)
# Compare two halves of the example data (odd vs even rows)
odd <- seq(1, nrow(lineup_example), by = 2)
# 50 resamples keep the example quick; use 1000 or more in an analysis
cmp <- compare_dpp(lineup_example[odd, ], lineup_example[-odd, ],
                   n_bootstrap = 50, seed = 1)
cmp
#> 
#> === DPP Comparison ===
#> 
#> Average DPP, procedure A:  0.6862 
#> Average DPP, procedure B:  0.7139 
#> Difference (A - B):        -0.0278  (negative = A better)
#> Bootstrap SE:              0.0310
#> 95% percentile interval:  [-0.0817, 0.0257]  (50 resamples)
